## Why Your Milk Goes Bad Two Days Before The Date On The Packet

You bought the packet on Monday. It says good until Sunday. On Thursday
evening you make tea and it splits in the cup. You check the date again.
Still three days left. You smell the packet. It is fine. You blame the
brand. The brand is probably not what went wrong.

## The date is a promise with a condition attached

Every shelf life printed on a food packet is calculated in a lab under
specific conditions. For milk, that condition is: kept at the correct
temperature, continuously, from the plant to your fridge.That printed
date is not a timer that counts down at a fixed rate. It is a prediction
of how long the product will last if the temperature holds.Milk is a
near-perfect food for bacteria. That is why it is chilled. Chilling does
not kill the bacteria — it slows them down. Let the temperature rise,
and they speed back up. Bring it back down, and they slow again, but the
growth that happened while it was warm has already happened. It does not
un-happen. So a packet that spent a few hours warm somewhere in its
journey arrives at your fridge biologically older than the date
suggests. The date says Sunday. The milk thinks it is Friday.

## Where the warm hours come from

There are four places in a milk chain where time gets stolen, and most
consumers only ever see the last one.

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **Between the animal and the chilling centre.** Fresh milk comes out
  warm. Until it reaches a chilling centre it is at its most vulnerable.
  If collection routes are long or delayed, the milk arriving at the
  plant already carries a bacterial load nothing downstream fully
  undoes.
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **In the plant and the tanker:** Usually the best-managed part. Big
  volumes, institutional handling on both ends.
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **In distribution:** This is where it breaks apart. One tanker becomes
  fifty vehicles going to five hundred shops. Some of those vehicles are
  properly refrigerated. Some are insulated boxes with ice. Some are a
  two-wheeler with a crate.
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **At the shop:** The packet sitting in a crate on the floor at eight
  in the morning waiting for someone to load it into the cooler. The
  cooler that was switched off overnight. The crate near the door in
  June.

## The one you can see

Next time you buy milk, look at where it is sitting. If the packets are
in a crate on the floor rather than inside a cooler, that milk has been
at room temperature for however long it has been there. On a Mumbai
morning in May, that is not a small thing.If the cooler is packed so
tightly that air cannot move, the packets in the middle are warmer than
the ones at the edge. Cooling works by moving air. A solid wall of
packets does not cool evenly. If the shop keeps the cooler door open for
convenience during the rush, everything inside is riding a temperature
roller coaster all day.None of this is the shopkeeper being careless.
Most of it is electricity cost, space, and habit. But it explains your
Thursday tea.

## What actually helps

- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **Buy from a shop with a proper cooler** and buy from inside it, not
  from the crate on the floor.
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **Buy later in your shopping trip**, not first, and go straight home.
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **Check the packet feel.** Cold to the touch means it has been cold.
  Room temperature means it has not been, at least recently.
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **Store it at the back of the fridge, not the door.** The fridge door
  is the warmest place in your fridge and swings every time you open it.
- ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyBhcmlhLWhpZGRlbj0idHJ1ZSIgdmlld2JveD0iMCAwIDUxMiA1MTIiIHhtbG5zPSJodHRwOi8vd3d3LnczLm9yZy8yMDAwL3N2ZyI+PHBhdGggZD0iTTI1NiA4QzExOSA4IDggMTE5IDggMjU2czExMSAyNDggMjQ4IDI0OCAyNDgtMTExIDI0OC0yNDhTMzkzIDggMjU2IDh6IiAvPjwvc3ZnPg==)
  **Boil it if you are unsure**, especially in summer. Generations of
  Indian households do this by instinct and the instinct is sound.

## The bigger picture

India produces an enormous amount of milk. We also lose an enormous
amount of it — not usually as visible spoilage, but as shortened shelf
life, quiet returns, and markdowns that get written off as retail
performance. Almost none of that is a production problem. It is a
temperature problem, and it happens in the gaps between the plant and
your kitchen. Those gaps are filled by cold chain — chilling centres,
refrigerated vehicles, cold rooms, and shop-level cooling that actually
stays on. Every one of them is invisible when it works. [Go Back](/blog)
